name: Business Manager Visa (経営・管理)
description: Everything about Japan's Business Manager visa (経営・管理): the status of residence for foreign entrepreneurs, company directors, and business executives operating in Japan. This visa underwent a major overhaul effective October 16, 2025, significantly raising the requirements for new applicants. The minimum capital investment increased from ¥5,000,000 to ¥30,000,000, a certified business plan is now mandatory, Japanese language proficiency is required, and applicants must demonstrate at least 3 years of management experience or a qualifying graduate degree. At least 1 full-time employee must be hired — they must be a Japanese national, Special Permanent Resident, or a foreigner with a Table 2 residence status (Permanent Resident, Spouse of Japanese National, Spouse of Permanent Resident, or Long-term Resident); work visa holders do not count. Transitional measures apply until October 16, 2028 for existing holders who obtained their visas before the overhaul. Duration ranges from 1 to 5 years and is renewable, with a path to permanent residence through the standard 10-year route. This visa is fundamentally different from a work visa — the holder must be actively managing or operating the business, not simply employed by it. Updated for 2026.
tagline: Establish and manage a business in Japan under the new 2025 framework
keyRequirement: ¥30,000,000+ capital investment, certified business plan, 3+ years management experience, Japanese language proficiency (Oct 2025 rules)
targetAudience: Foreign entrepreneurs planning to establish a new business in Japan
Company directors and executives of Japan-based subsidiaries
Professionals transitioning from Engineer/Specialist visa to start their own business
International business owners seeking to expand operations into the Japanese market
Existing Business Manager visa holders navigating the October 2025 rule changes

eligibility.label: Minimum capital investment of ¥30,000,000 (effective October 2025)
eligibility.description: The business must have invested capital of at least ¥30,000,000. For corporations, this means paid-in capital (資本金の額) or total contributions; capital reserves and retained surplus do not count. For sole proprietors, the total amount invested in the business (office, one year of employee salaries, equipment) must reach ¥30,000,000. The requirement applies even to managers who are not the owner, and where multiple companies are involved, at least one must independently meet the ¥30,000,000 threshold. The capital must be verifiable through business registration documents and bank records, and the source of funds is scrutinized to ensure legitimacy.
warnings: The October 2025 overhaul raised the capital requirement 6x to ¥30,000,000 — applications under the old ¥5,000,000 threshold are no longer accepted for new applicants
Capital reserves and surplus (資本準備金・剰余金) do NOT count toward the ¥30,000,000 threshold — only paid-in capital or equivalent direct investment

eligibility.label: Employ at least 1 qualifying full-time employee
eligibility.description: The business must hire at least one full-time employee who is: a Japanese national (日本人), a Special Permanent Resident (特別永住者), or a foreigner holding a Table 2 residence status — specifically Permanent Resident (永住者), Spouse of Japanese National (日本人の配偶者等), Spouse of Permanent Resident (永住者の配偶者等), or Long-term Resident (定住者). Foreign nationals on Table 1 work visas (e.g., Engineer/Specialist in Humanities, Skilled Labor) do NOT count toward this requirement. Full-time is defined as: regular scheduled work, 5+ days per week, 217+ days per year, 30+ hours per week, and enrolled in employment insurance (雇用保険). Secondment (在籍出向), dispatch (派遣), and contract/outsourcing (請負) workers do not count — the employee must be directly employed.
warnings: Foreign employees on Table 1 work visas (Engineer/Specialist, Skilled Labor, etc.) do NOT count toward the minimum employee requirement
Secondment, dispatch, and contract workers do not count — the qualifying employee must be directly employed full-time
Full-time threshold: 5+ days/week, 217+ days/year, 30+ hours/week, enrolled in employment insurance

eligibility.label: Business plan reviewed by a Japanese-licensed professional
eligibility.description: A comprehensive business plan must be evaluated by one of the following Japanese-licensed professionals: 中小企業診断士 (SME Management Consultant), 公認会計士 (Certified Public Accountant), or 税理士 (Tax Accountant). The reviewer must be externally engaged — a company officer or employee cannot serve as the reviewer. Foreign professional equivalents (e.g., a US CPA without Japanese license) do not qualify. This is a mandatory requirement under the October 2025 overhaul; previously a business plan was recommended but certification was not required.
warnings: Foreign professional licenses (e.g., US CPA) do not qualify — the reviewer must hold a Japanese license
The reviewing professional cannot be a company officer or employee — must be external and independent

eligibility.label: 3+ years of management experience OR a qualifying graduate degree
eligibility.description: Applicants must satisfy one of two conditions: (1) a doctoral, master's, or professional degree related to business management or operations (経営管理に関する博士・修士・専門職学位), or (2) 3 or more years of experience in business management or operations. Startup preparation activity (起業準備活動) counts toward the 3-year experience period. Passive investment or remote management from outside Japan does not qualify.
warnings: Passive investment or remote management from outside Japan does not qualify — immigration verifies active, in-person business management
A qualifying graduate degree (doctoral, master's, or professional degree in business management) fully satisfies this requirement in place of experience

eligibility.label: Japanese language proficiency at B2 equivalent — applicant OR a qualifying full-time employee (mandatory under October 2025 rules)
eligibility.description: The applicant or at least one full-time employee of the business must hold Japanese language proficiency at B2 equivalent (日本語教育の参照枠 B2相当以上). This can be demonstrated by any of the following: JLPT N2 or higher, BJT Business Japanese Test score of 400 or above, 20+ years of mid- or long-term residence in Japan, graduation from a Japanese university or higher education institution (including vocational schools 専門学校), or completion of Japanese compulsory education plus graduation from high school. For the language requirement only, Table 1 visa holders (work visa holders) may count as a qualifying 常勤職員 — unlike the employment requirement, where Table 1 holders are excluded. This requirement was not in place before October 2025.
warnings: Japanese language proficiency (B2 equivalent / JLPT N2) is now mandatory — either the applicant OR a qualifying full-time employee must satisfy this
Note the distinction: for the LANGUAGE requirement, Table 1 visa holders (work visa employees) CAN count; for the EMPLOYMENT requirement, they cannot

eligibility.label: Dedicated physical office space in Japan (home office not permitted)
eligibility.description: The business must have adequate dedicated office space that matches the scale of the business. Home offices are not permitted in principle (原則として認められません). Virtual offices are also not accepted. The office must be properly registered as the business address and verifiable through the lease agreement and company registration.
warnings: Home office is not permitted in principle under the October 2025 rules — a dedicated commercial office is required

duration.initialDetail: Duration determined by business scale, financial stability, and immigration officer assessment.
duration.extension: Renewable — must demonstrate ongoing business operations, employee retention, and tax compliance at each renewal
duration.maxTotalDetail: Path to permanent residence through the 10-year standard route.

fees.applicationDetail: Certificate of Eligibility (COE): ¥0 (free). Visa issuance: ¥3,000 (single-entry) or ¥6,000 (multiple-entry).
fees.extension: ¥4,000 for extension of stay or change of status
fees.notes: These are government fees only. Business setup costs (incorporation, registered agent, office lease, professional certification of business plan) are substantial additional expenses. FY2026 fee increases have been announced — check the ISA website for current schedules.

incomeRequirement.notes: The ¥30,000,000 is a capital investment requirement, not an income requirement. However, the business must also demonstrate financial sustainability and the ability to generate revenue. Immigration officers evaluate whether the business can support the visa holder and employees.
proofMethods: Business bank account statements showing capitalization
Company registration documents showing paid-in capital
Investment records and fund transfer documentation
Certified business plan with financial projections

documents.name: Valid Passport
documents.description: Must be valid for at least 6 months beyond the intended period of stay

documents.name: Certificate of Eligibility (COE)
documents.description: Filed at the regional immigration bureau. For the Business Manager visa, the applicant or a designated representative in Japan (such as a registered agent or lawyer) typically handles the filing since there is no employer sponsor.
tips: Many applicants hire an immigration lawyer (行政書士 or 弁護士) to handle the COE application
Processing is typically 2-3 months but can take longer for new businesses without track record

documents.name: Certified Business Plan
documents.nameLocal: 事業計画書（専門家認証済み）
documents.description: A detailed business plan covering the business model, market analysis, revenue projections, staffing plan, and operational details. Must be certified by a professional expert (CPA, tax accountant, or SME management consultant). This is a new mandatory requirement under the October 2025 rules.
tips: The business plan should be realistic and conservative — overly optimistic projections raise red flags
Include clear financial projections for at least 3 years
Explain how the business contributes to Japan's economy (job creation, tax revenue, innovation)

documents.name: Company Registration Documents
documents.description: Certificate of registered matters (登記事項証明書) from the Legal Affairs Bureau showing the company's legal registration, directors, capital, and registered address in Japan. If the company is not yet registered, documents showing the incorporation process may be accepted.

documents.name: Proof of Capital Investment (¥30,000,000+)
documents.description: Bank statements, fund transfer records, and company financial documents proving that at least ¥30,000,000 has been invested as capital. The source of funds must be transparent and legitimate.
tips: Prepare documentation showing the origin of funds — immigration may investigate fund sources
Wire transfers from overseas accounts should have clear paper trails

documents.name: Office Lease Agreement
documents.description: Lease contract for the business premises in Japan. The office must be a proper commercial space — residential addresses and virtual offices are typically not accepted. The lease should be in the company's name.

documents.name: Employee Employment Contracts
documents.description: Employment contracts for at least 1 qualifying full-time employee: a Japanese national, Special Permanent Resident, or a foreigner with Table 2 residence status (Permanent Resident, Spouse of Japanese National, Spouse of Permanent Resident, or Long-term Resident). Must show job title, duties, salary, work schedule, and enrollment in employment insurance. Also include documentation confirming the employee's nationality or residence status. Foreign employees on Table 1 work visas do not count.

documents.name: Proof of Management Experience or Qualifying Degree
documents.nameLocal: 経営経験証明書／学位証明書
documents.description: Either: (A) documentation proving 3+ years of business management experience — employment certificates showing executive or management titles, company registration showing directorship, or records of startup preparation activity (起業準備活動); OR (B) a doctoral, master's, or professional degree certificate related to business management or operations, plus official transcripts.
tips: If using experience: include references from business partners or board members who can verify your management role
Startup preparation activity (起業準備活動) counts toward the 3-year experience period — document it with records of market research, business registration steps, meetings with advisors, etc.
If using a qualifying degree: provide the degree certificate, transcripts, and a translation if not in Japanese or English

documents.name: Japanese Language Proficiency Certificate (B2 equivalent)
documents.description: Proof of Japanese language proficiency at B2 equivalent (日本語教育の参照枠 B2相当以上), from either the applicant or a qualifying full-time employee. Accepted evidence: JLPT N2 or higher certificate, BJT Business Japanese Test result sheet showing 400+ score, certificate of 20+ years mid/long-term residence in Japan, graduation certificate from a Japanese university or vocational school (専門学校), or certificate of completion of Japanese compulsory education plus high school graduation. For language requirement purposes, Table 1 visa holders may count as qualifying employees.

documents.name: Passport-Size Photo
documents.description: 4cm x 3cm, taken within the last 6 months, white background

applicationSteps.title: Prepare Capital and Business Plan
applicationSteps.description: Secure the ¥30,000,000+ capital investment and develop a comprehensive business plan. Engage a professional expert (CPA, tax accountant, or SME management consultant) to certify the business plan. This is the most time-consuming preparatory step under the new rules.
applicationSteps.duration: 1-3 months for business plan development and certification
tips: Start with the business plan — the certification process itself can take several weeks
Research the Japanese market thoroughly — immigration evaluates the viability of the business
Consider hiring a Japanese business consultant familiar with immigration requirements

applicationSteps.title: Incorporate the Business in Japan
applicationSteps.description: Register the company with the Legal Affairs Bureau (法務局). Choose the appropriate corporate structure (株式会社 for a standard corporation or 合同会社 for an LLC). Deposit the required capital, obtain a company seal (印鑑), open a corporate bank account, and secure office space.
tips: Many foreign entrepreneurs use a 合同会社 (LLC) for simpler setup, but 株式会社 may carry more credibility with immigration
You may need a local representative or registered agent if you are not yet in Japan
Corporate bank accounts for new foreign-owned companies can be difficult to open — start this process early

applicationSteps.title: Hire Required Employee(s) and Set Up Operations
applicationSteps.description: Hire at least 1 full-time employee who is a Japanese national or permanent resident. Enroll the employee in social insurance (health insurance and pension). Set up the physical office, business operations, and any necessary licenses.
tips: The employee must be enrolled in shakai hoken (social insurance) — this is verified by immigration
Foreign employees on work visas do not count toward the requirement under the new rules

applicationSteps.title: File COE Application at Immigration Bureau
applicationSteps.description: Submit the complete COE application at the regional immigration bureau. Include: certified business plan, company registration documents, proof of ¥30,000,000+ capital, office lease, employee contracts, management experience documentation, and Japanese language certificate. Many applicants engage an immigration lawyer (行政書士) to handle this step.
tips: Professional representation by a licensed 行政書士 (administrative scrivener) or immigration lawyer is strongly recommended
New businesses without a track record face more scrutiny — the strength of the business plan is critical

applicationSteps.title: Obtain Visa and Enter Japan (or Change Status)
applicationSteps.description: If applying from abroad: receive the COE, apply for the visa at your local Japanese embassy, and enter Japan. If already in Japan on another visa (e.g., Engineer/Specialist): apply for change of status at the immigration bureau. Critical timing: if transitioning from an employment visa, file the change of status before your current employment ends to avoid a gap in legal status.
applicationSteps.duration: Visa processing: 5-10 working days (from abroad) | Status change: 2-4 weeks (in Japan)
tips: If transitioning from Engineer/Specialist visa: file the startup notification and status change application before your employment ends
A gap of more than 3 months without valid status creates serious legal complications
warnings: If transitioning from another visa, a gap of more than 3 months without valid status creates serious legal complications that can affect all future visa applications

applicationSteps.title: Begin Operations and Maintain Compliance
applicationSteps.description: Once the visa is issued, begin active business operations. Maintain compliance with all tax filing, social insurance, and employee requirements. Immigration evaluates ongoing business viability at each renewal — the business must demonstrate sustained operations, revenue, and employment.
tips: File all tax returns on time — late or missing filings are a red flag at renewal
Keep detailed financial records — immigration may request profit and loss statements at renewal
Maintain the full-time employee requirement continuously — losing the employee can affect renewal

processingTime.governmentReviewDetail: Business setup: 1–3 months. COE processing: 2–3 months. Visa issuance: 5–10 working days.
processingTime.notes: The total timeline from initial planning to visa issuance is typically longer for Business Manager visas than for employment-based visas, due to the business setup requirements. New businesses without an operating history face additional scrutiny that can extend processing. Published guidelines recommend engaging professional support (immigration lawyer and business consultant) to avoid delays.

restrictions: Must be actively engaged in managing or operating the business — cannot be a passive investor
Cannot work as an employee of another company on this visa
Business activities must match those described in the visa application and business plan
workPermission.notes: The Business Manager visa authorizes the holder to manage and operate their business in Japan. This is fundamentally different from an employment visa — the holder must be an active manager or director, not simply an employee. Passive investment without active management does not qualify. The holder may operate multiple businesses.

faqs.question: What changed with the October 2025 overhaul?
faqs.answer: The October 16, 2025 changes (effective date: 令和7年10月16日) significantly raised the bar for new Business Manager visa applicants. Key changes: (1) minimum capital increased from ¥5,000,000 to ¥30,000,000 — a 6x increase; (2) a business plan review by a Japanese-licensed 中小企業診断士, 公認会計士, or 税理士 is now mandatory; (3) at least 3 years of management experience OR a qualifying graduate degree in business management is required; (4) Japanese language proficiency at B2 equivalent (JLPT N2 / BJT 400+) is now mandatory — either the applicant OR a qualifying full-time employee must satisfy this; (5) the qualifying full-time employee must be a Japanese national, Special Permanent Resident, or Table 2 residence status holder — Table 1 work visa holders do not count; (6) home office is not permitted in principle. Applications filed before October 16, 2025 are assessed under the old rules. A 3-year grace period runs until October 16, 2028 for existing holders.

faqs.question: Do the new rules affect existing Business Manager visa holders?
faqs.answer: A 3-year grace period applies until October 16, 2028 (令和10年10月16日). Existing holders who obtained their Business Manager visa before October 16, 2025 may renew during this transition period, and ISA will consider overall business status even if the new criteria are not yet fully met. Separately, holders of the startup visa (特定活動44号→経営・管理) who received their certification before October 15, 2025 may transition to Business Manager status under the old rules. During the transition period, confirm your specific situation with the immigration bureau or a licensed 行政書士.

faqs.question: Can I transition from Engineer/Specialist visa to Business Manager?
faqs.answer: Yes, but the timing is critical. File the startup notification and status change application while still employed — before your current employment ends. A gap of more than 3 months without valid status creates legal complications. You must meet all the new requirements: ¥30,000,000 capital, certified business plan, management experience or qualifying degree, Japanese language proficiency, and at least 1 qualifying full-time employee (Japanese national, Special Permanent Resident, or Table 2 residence status holder).

faqs.question: What type of business plan review is required?
faqs.answer: The business plan must be reviewed by one of three Japanese-licensed professionals: a 中小企業診断士 (SME Management Consultant), a 公認会計士 (Certified Public Accountant), or a 税理士 (Tax Accountant). Two strict conditions apply: (1) the reviewer must hold a Japanese license — foreign equivalents such as a US CPA do not qualify; (2) the reviewer must be external and independent — a company officer or employee cannot serve as reviewer. This is a new mandatory requirement under the October 2025 overhaul; previously a business plan was recommended but formal review was not required.

faqs.question: Is ¥30,000,000 the minimum for all business types?
faqs.answer: Yes. ¥30,000,000 is the minimum capital investment for the Business Manager visa under the October 2025 rules, regardless of business type or industry. There is no lower threshold for smaller businesses or specific sectors. For corporations, only paid-in capital counts — capital reserves and surplus do not. For sole proprietors, the total invested in the business (office, one year of employee salaries, equipment) must reach ¥30,000,000. Where multiple companies are involved, at least one must independently meet the ¥30,000,000 threshold. The source of funds must be transparent and legitimate.

faqs.question: Why do foreign work visa holders not count toward the employee requirement?
faqs.answer: Under the October 2025 overhaul, the qualifying employee must be a Japanese national (日本人), Special Permanent Resident (特別永住者), or a foreigner with Table 2 residence status: Permanent Resident (永住者), Spouse of Japanese National (日本人の配偶者等), Spouse of Permanent Resident (永住者の配偶者等), or Long-term Resident (定住者). Foreign nationals on Table 1 work visas — such as Engineer/Specialist in Humanities, Skilled Labor, or other employment-based categories — do not count. The rationale is that the requirement targets stable, long-term residents of Japan rather than holders of employer-dependent visas. Foreign employees on work visas can still be hired, but they do not satisfy the minimum qualifying employee requirement.

faqs.question: Can I operate the business remotely from outside Japan?
faqs.answer: No. The Business Manager visa requires active, in-person management of the business in Japan. Passive ownership or remote management from abroad does not qualify. Additionally, being absent from Japan for more than 50% of your permitted stay period is treated as a negative factor at renewal — ISA may determine the holder is not actively engaged in business management and deny renewal.

faqs.question: What level of Japanese language is required?
faqs.answer: The requirement is B2 equivalent on the Japanese Language Education Reference Framework (日本語教育の参照枠 B2相当以上). It can be satisfied by the applicant or by a qualifying full-time employee of the business. Accepted proof methods: JLPT N2 or higher, BJT Business Japanese Test score of 400+, 20+ years of mid/long-term residence in Japan, graduation from a Japanese university or vocational school, or completion of Japanese compulsory education plus high school graduation. Important distinction: for the language requirement only, Table 1 visa holders (work visa employees) may count as qualifying 常勤職員 — unlike the employment requirement where they are excluded. This requirement was not in place before October 2025.

faqs.question: How does this visa lead to permanent residence?
faqs.answer: The standard route is 10 consecutive years of residence in Japan, with at least 5 years on a qualifying visa. Business Manager holders can also qualify under HSP (Highly Skilled Professional) criteria in the Advanced Business Management category (i)(c) if they accumulate 70+ points, which can accelerate the PR timeline to 1-3 years. Tax compliance and social insurance payment history are scrutinized at the PR application stage.

faqs.question: Can multiple foreign nationals co-manage the same business?
faqs.answer: Yes, but each co-manager must independently satisfy the Business Manager visa requirements, including the ¥30,000,000 capital threshold and management experience or degree. Each co-manager must also have a clearly defined role and receive compensation commensurate with their position — ISA verifies that each person's management role is genuine and not duplicative. Tax and social insurance compliance is verified individually at each renewal.

faqs.question: What happens at renewal if the business is not profitable?
faqs.answer: Immigration officers evaluate the business's ongoing viability at each renewal. Temporary losses are not automatically disqualifying — early-stage businesses often operate at a loss. However, the business must demonstrate ongoing operations, employee retention, tax compliance, and a credible path to sustainability. Persistent losses without clear recovery plans, failure to maintain the qualifying employee, tax delinquency, or social insurance non-compliance can result in renewal denial. Absence from Japan for more than 50% of the permitted stay period is also a negative factor.

tips: Engage a licensed immigration lawyer (行政書士 or 弁護士) early — the Business Manager visa application is significantly more complex than employment-based visas

Japanese language proficiency at JLPT N2 is now mandatory — either you or a full-time employee must hold N2-equivalent proficiency. If you are not a Japanese speaker, hiring an N2-level Japanese national or permanent-resident employee can satisfy this requirement
Build the business plan with immigration requirements in mind — a certified plan that demonstrates job creation, tax contribution, and economic impact strengthens the application
Open the corporate bank account early — Japanese banks are notoriously difficult for new foreign-owned companies, and the process can take weeks
If transitioning from an employment visa, file the status change before your employment ends — the 3-month gap rule is strictly enforced
Maintain meticulous financial records from day one — immigration reviews profit and loss statements, tax filings, and employee records at each renewal
The ¥30,000,000 capital must be verifiable and its source transparent — prepare documentation showing the origin of funds
Ensure the full-time employee is enrolled in social insurance (shakai hoken) — this is verified by immigration during the application and at renewal

communityTips.tip: If you are on an Engineer/Specialist visa and planning to start a business, begin the Business Manager visa preparation at least 6-8 months before you plan to leave your current employer. The business setup, plan certification, COE filing, and status change processing all take time. Leaving your job before the status change is approved creates a dangerous gap.

Opening a corporate bank account for a new foreign-owned company in Japan is one of the biggest practical challenges. Major banks (MUFG, SMBC, Mizuho) often require an established business history. Consider starting with a smaller regional bank or an online bank like GMO Aozora or PayPay Bank, which tend to have more accessible requirements for new businesses.

A licensed 行政書士 (administrative scrivener) specializing in immigration is invaluable for the Business Manager visa. They handle the COE application, ensure documentation is complete, and communicate directly with the immigration bureau. Fees typically range from ¥200,000-¥500,000 depending on complexity, but the investment significantly reduces rejection risk.

If you hold a Business Manager visa obtained before October 16, 2025, a 3-year grace period applies until October 16, 2028. During this period, ISA considers overall business status at renewal even if the new criteria are not yet fully met. Holders of the startup visa (特定活動44号) who received certification before October 15, 2025 can transition to Business Manager under the old rules. Confirm your specific situation with a licensed 行政書士 — the transitional provisions vary by case.

JLPT N2-level proficiency is now mandatory for the Business Manager visa — but the requirement applies to either the applicant OR a full-time employee. If you are not a Japanese speaker, hiring an N2-level Japanese national or permanent-resident employee satisfies this rule. If you plan to satisfy it yourself, reaching N2 typically takes 1.5-2 years of regular study from zero. The JLPT is offered only twice a year (July and December), so plan your test dates accordingly.

agencySteps.agencyFullName: Immigration Services Agency of Japan (出入国在留管理庁)
agencySteps.description: Employer or representative files Certificate of Eligibility application.
tips: Processing varies by regional bureau — Tokyo is typically slower

agencySteps.description: Submit COE with passport and application form at nearest Japanese embassy.

postArrivalSteps.title: Residence Card
postArrivalSteps.deadline: Issued at airport (Narita, Haneda, Kansai, Chubu)
postArrivalSteps.description: Your residence card (在留カード) is issued upon arrival at designated airports. At other ports of entry, visit your local ward office within 14 days.
tips: Always carry your residence card — it is legally required

postArrivalSteps.title: Ward Office Registration (住民届)
postArrivalSteps.description: Register your address at the local ward/city office. Required for health insurance enrollment and bank account opening.
tips: Bring residence card, passport, and proof of address

pathsTo.name: Engineer/Specialist in Humanities/International Services Visa
pathsTo.requirements: Hold Engineer/Specialist status and meet all Business Manager visa requirements: ¥30,000,000 capital, certified business plan, 3+ years management experience, Japanese language proficiency at JLPT N2 level (either the applicant or a full-time employee), and 1+ full-time Japanese/permanent-resident employee.
pathsTo.timeline: Business setup: 1-3 months + COE/status change: 2-3 months; total 3-6 months
pathsTo.notes: The most common transition path to Business Manager visa. The October 2025 overhaul makes this a significantly more demanding transition than before. Critical: file the startup notification and status change before your current employment ends to avoid a gap in legal status. Begin preparations at least 6-8 months in advance.
